Proof 4.1 is correct: count endpoints using the upper bridge arcs alone, which partition L intersect S into pairs. The sole upper bridge crossing P_+ once contributes one endpoint to S_i; all other upper bridges contribute zero or two. Therefore r_i=1+2m_i is odd. The lower arcs partition the SAME endpoint set; adding both systems double-counts every point, which is the error in the reported even-parity argument. The explicitly constructed factor sphere adds one cap endpoint, giving n_i=(r_i+1)/2=m_i+1 and n1+n2=b+1. Independently reviewed all current steps, actual normalization and fourteen prerequisites, plus Negami–Okita Lemma 3-3/proposition 3-5 and Schultens comparison. No repair warranted; see detailed companion report.
